correctness.rationale: Private-neighbor characterization is local on a radius-two/five-column window with absent-column PAD rather than zero mask. An exact 625-state integer potential satisfies R(s)≥popcount(newmask)-1+R(t), R(START)=0, R(terminal)≥0; telescoping proves every inclusion-minimal dominating set of L_n has size ≤n. Explicit singleton-column witnesses attain n. All gain-tight accepting paths are compared in a synchronous finite product with six periodic languages; independently replayed potential converges in 2 Bellman rounds and finite product enumerates exactly 41 reachable states/46 transitions with equality of every acceptance predicate. This finite-state identity proves all lengths, not mere finite enumeration. Independent graph-subset enumeration n=1..10 matches counts n=1:2; n even≥2:6; n odd≥3:4.

originality.rationale: Sahbi arXiv:2610.03785v2, Section 8 Theorem 8.1, proves the scalar Gamma(P_m square P_n)=ceil(mn/2), deriving it from classical bipartite Gamma=alpha. It does not enumerate the full maximizing inclusion-minimal dominating families on the two-row ladder. OEIS A290379 records total minimal dominating sets for ladders, not the top coefficient of the cardinality polynomial, and the 2024 grid paper concerns minimum rather than maximum minimal sets. The new equality-case word classification is stronger than the known scalar theorem, and no published Resultary comparison implied it.
residual_risks: A different historic enumeration of irredundant dominating families may have escaped indexing; no search proves novelty conclusively.

value.rationale: An exact, natural, complete classification of all largest minimal dominating configurations for the canonical width-two strip, including a surprising even/odd oscillation with six versus four extremizers. It gives the leading coefficient of the minimal-domination polynomial and a finite-state certificate usable for related strip enumeration; not just restating the known upper-domination number.

limitations: Finite state certificate checks 625 states/all transitions and reachable-language closure; n=1 is separate boundary of two sets, theorem n>=2.
Cartesian ladder only, not strong-product strips or wider grids.
